newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices ease ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices ease ahead of weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices eased Friday ahead of the weekend as forecasters called for milder weather in the Midwest, industry sources said.
Gulf Coast prices slipped about three cents to the mid-$2.30s, with Henry Hub, La., quoted mostly in the $2.34-2.38 range.

The Friday morning outage at Texas Utilities' 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak nuclear unit 2 in Glen Rose, Texas, had virtually no impact on the market since temperatures are cooler in the region, traders said.
TU said the unit would likely restart early Saturday.
In the Midcontinent, prices softened by more than five cents to the low-to-mid $2.20s, pressured by forecasts for milder temperatures.
Fueled by a strong heating demand, some early buyers on Northern, however, pushed Demarcation prices into the high-$2.30s. As trading progressed, prices fell back into the high-$2.20s.
Cooler Texas weather pushed prices in the Permian basin into the $2.16-2.21 range, down at least 10 cents from Thursday's levels.
Similary at the southern California border, the weekend market fell into the low-$2.20s, down more than 10 cents.
At the New York city-gate, where temperatures are expected to drop to below-normal levels this weekend, prices were mostly steady in the $2.75-$2.80 area.
